name: rat-king
about: Chain ragdoll body for the Rat King mini-boss (24-bone rat rig, shared with the plain rat and the crow). 13 capsules: hips (root, pelvis to chest), chest (with spine), head (neck to bite_tip; head and jaw ride on it), tail_a, tail_b, and 4 legs x (upper, lower). Bones without a body (root, spine, head, jaw, bite_tip, tail_2, tail_4, the paws) follow their parent bone in the scene graph. Every number is here; src/chain.mjs holds none.
placeholder_note: radii, masses, joint limits and motor scales are PLACEHOLDERS to tune on Dom's phone and the clips; only the bone positions are measured.
scale_source: Armagedom PR #435 Web/src/data/creatureChainRows.json row rat-king: modelScale 6 (the cross-check of 2026-10-28 found the old x3 here came from the plain rat's definition; the rat king is x6). The actor wrapper's character 1.265 / visual 1.3225 multipliers are NOT applied here: the game applies them to the sim root. rat-king.glb lengths equal original-rat.glb's (both measured at model scale 1).
mass_assumption: placeholder, ASSUMPTION: the old row was 37 kg at x3. Scaling the body by 2 multiplies its volume by 2^3 = 8, so every mass is multiplied by the cube of the scale ratio (6/3)^3 = 8, giving 296 kg total (a 1.8 m rat; by real-rat density it would be about 64 kg, but the Rat King is a mini-boss and should fall heavy, so the old 'heavy' bias is kept). Still far heavier than the 6 kg crow. Tune against how heavy the fall should feel.
radius_source: radii retuned 2026-10-28 toward the game-measured radiusModel (Armagedom PR #435: median distance of skin-weighted side-wall vertices from the bone axis, model units): hips 0.036 -> 0.064 (game 0.1115), chest 0.036 -> 0.057 (0.0572), head 0.027 -> 0.042 (0.0419), tail_a 0.011 -> 0.055 (0.0631), hind uppers 0.011 -> 0.0545 (0.098 / 0.083). Limits (largest radius that keeps every non-adjacent pair of capsules clear by 3 mm at rest): hips by the front upper legs (leg_FL_up / leg_FR_up sit 0.04 model units off the spine), hind uppers and tail_a by each other. Front uppers (game 0.013) and the lower legs (game 0.007 / 0.0055, thinner than the 0.009 placeholder) are unchanged.
inertia_source: data/ragdoll-role-table.json motor.inertia_multiplier (M1 finding), same value as the humanoid rows
hinge_flex_z_source: own: the creature faces +z. On this rig every leg is elbow-shaped: the joint at the shin bone sits behind both the hip and the paw (hind: hip z -0.071, shin -0.104, paw -0.053; front: hip 0.047, shin 0.022, paw 0.082), so the lower leg folds forward (+z) like a human elbow, for hind and front alike.
